title: Orthogonality and Trivialization of the Change-of-Lagrangian Cocycle
body_html:
Orthogonality and Trivialization of the Change-of-Lagrangian Cocycle

This is the summary node for the finite-field Weil-index calculation. The proof is split into smaller nodes so that each step can be cited separately. It separates two facts: the formal base-Lagrangian coboundary identity for chosen Lagrangian intertwiners, and Gérardin's linearization of the full projective symplectic Weil cocycle.

Setup

Let \(k\) be a finite field of odd order \(q\), let \((E,j)\) be a nondegenerate symplectic \(k\)-space of dimension \(2m\), and put \(i=j/2\). Fix a nontrivial additive character \(\xi:k\to R^\times\), where \(\operatorname{char}R\neq \operatorname{char}k\).

For each Lagrangian \(L\subset E\), let \(\mathcal S_L\) be the Schrödinger model of the finite Heisenberg representation with central character \(\xi\).

Raw Transition

For Lagrangians \(L,L'\), the raw change-of-Lagrangian map is

$$ (\mathcal F_{L,L'}\varphi)(v) = \sum_{a\in L/(L\cap L')} \xi(i(a,v))\varphi(v+a). $$

By Change-of-Lagrangian Intertwiner for Finite Schrödinger Models, this is a well-defined \(H(E,j)\)-intertwiner

$$ \mathcal F_{L,L'}:\mathcal S_{L'}\to\mathcal S_L. $$

It is nonzero. By One-Dimensional Hom Line for Finite Schrödinger Models, the intertwiner line is one-dimensional:

$$ \operatorname{Hom}_{H(E,j)}(\mathcal S_{L'},\mathcal S_L) =R\cdot \mathcal F_{L,L'}. $$

Orthogonality

Set

$$ d_{L,L'}:=m-\dim_k(L\cap L'). $$

By Orthogonality of Change-of-Lagrangian Intertwiners,

$$ \mathcal F_{L,L'}\circ \mathcal F_{L',L} = q^{d_{L,L'}}\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal S_L}. $$

Thus every \(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\) is an isomorphism.

Weil-Index Cocycle

For three Lagrangians \(L,L',L''\), define \(\gamma(L,L',L'')\in R^\times\) by

$$ \mathcal F_{L,L'}\circ \mathcal F_{L',L''} = \gamma(L,L',L'')\mathcal F_{L,L''}. $$

By Finite Weil-Index Cocycle for Lagrangian Transitions, these scalars satisfy the cocycle identity

$$ \gamma(L,L',L'')\gamma(L,L'',L''') = \gamma(L',L'',L''')\gamma(L,L',L'''). $$

This \(\gamma\) is the finite Weil-index cocycle for the chosen raw normalization of the transition maps. It should be distinguished from the finite quadratic Weil index Finite Quadratic Weil Index, which is a normalized Gauss sum attached to a finite quadratic module. Gérardin's formulas connect the two by identifying Fourier-normalization constants with quadratic Gauss-sum Weil indices.

Base-Lagrangian Trivialization

Fix a base Lagrangian \(L_0\). Define

$$ c_{L,L'}:=\gamma(L,L',L_0). $$

By Base-Lagrangian Trivialization of the Finite Weil-Index Cocycle,

$$ \gamma(L,L',L'')=c_{L,L'}c_{L',L''}c_{L,L''}^{-1}. $$

Also \(c_{L,L}=1\).

Therefore the normalized maps

$$ \widetilde{\mathcal F}_{L,L'}:=c_{L,L'}^{-1}\mathcal F_{L,L'} $$

compose strictly:

$$ \widetilde{\mathcal F}_{L,L'}\circ \widetilde{\mathcal F}_{L',L''} = \widetilde{\mathcal F}_{L,L''}. $$

An explicit formula for \(c_{L,L'}\) is

$$ c_{L,L'} = \sum_{\substack{ a\in L'/(L'\cap L_0)\\ b\in L/(L\cap L')\\ a+b\in L_0 }} \xi(i(a,b)). $$

No \(q^{1/2}\) or external metaplectic cover is needed for this base-Lagrangian trivialization.

Gérardin Linearization

Gérardin's proof of the finite-field linearization is recorded in Gérardin Linearization of the Finite Symplectic Weil Cocycle. Its starting point is the projective action of \(S(E,j)\) on the unique Heisenberg representation. The obstruction is a projective group cocycle on \(S(E,j)\), not merely the three-Lagrangian scalar \(\gamma(L,L',L'')\).

The proof has two parts. First, the Heisenberg representation is extended over the parabolic stabilizer of a maximal isotropic subspace. Since this parabolic contains a \(p\)-Sylow subgroup of \(S(E,j)\), Gérardin's \(p\)-Sylow criterion Projective Cocycle Linearization Criterion for Finite Heisenberg Representations implies that the global projective cocycle is trivial. Second, the concrete Witt model fixes the normalization of the extension by Fourier transform and Gaussian sums, yielding formulas (2.10)-(2.18) in Gérardin.

Interpretation

The raw intertwiners \(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\) do not compose strictly in general; their defect is the Weil-index cocycle \(\gamma\). Over a finite field, this cocycle is a coboundary after fixing \(L_0\), so the Lagrangian Schrödinger models admit a compatible system of transition maps. The remaining question for \(p\)-adic lattice-model transitions is not this finite Lagrangian cocycle, but the separate \(p\)-adic metaplectic splitting behavior.
